text:
sana: Heads-up — working on envelope design for private deployments. Quick set of questions: DEK/KEK separation recommendations, acceptable KMS call frequency, caching TTL + splay/backoff patterns, RBAC for KEK ops, and audit logging for unwrap/rotation events. Any gotchas?

kevin: FYI we have a precedent in hosted where DEK cache default is 10m. For private we allowed up to 1h for lower-sensitivity tenants, but ops pushed back for high-risk customers. Tradeoff is obvious: fewer KMS calls vs larger blast radius.

ashok: Pattern we use: keep DEKs short-lived in local memory + store encrypted DEK blob in DB. Only call KMS to unwrap on cold miss. So KMS call rate ~= cache-miss rate (not per-request). Recommend jittered TTL: base_ttl + random(0, base_ttl/8) to avoid thundering herd.

jess: +1. For RBAC: put KEKs in customer-controlled KMS when possible, grant only the service principal and a tiny set of emergency human principals. Forward unwrap/decrypt audit logs to central SIEM and attach request metadata (caller, ip, request-id).

sana: How should we quantify blast radius for cache compromise (e.g., instance mem leak)? Any numeric guidance?

kevin: Depends on DEK granularity. Per-object DEKs -> blast radius = single object. Per-tenant DEK -> blast radius = whole tenant. Per-shard is a middle ground. Choose per-object for PHI or crypto-keys. Otherwise per-tenant/per-prefix for perf.

ashok: Rotation ops: lazy rewrap recommended. When KEK rotates, new writes produce DEKs wrapped with new KEK; reads must support both old and new KEKs during transition. Keep a rewrap worker to catch up. Consider double-wrap metadata: store KEK-version alongside encrypted DEK.

jess: Incident response: if KEK is suspected compromised -> immediately revoke key, rotate to new KEK, and mark affected DEKs as needing rewrap. Prep a playbook: snapshot affected blobs, run offline rewrap, notify customers. This is heavy and slow.

sec-bot: ALERT: KMS unwrap rate spike detected for project-redwood-prod, rule=kms_unwrap_spike_v1, severity=medium.

ops-liz: On caching layers: local in-memory LRU w/ TTL for lowest latency + optional Redis shared cache for cross-instance reuse. Shared cache only stores encrypted DEK blobs (safe), but treat shared cache as an additional attack surface—monitor access and consider encrypting cache values with a cache-specific key.

ashok: Add circuit-breaker around unwrap calls and exponential backoff on KMS errors. Also implement a token-bucket limiter per-instance to smooth bursts hitting KMS.

jess: Audit log content suggestions: include DEK fingerprint (sha256 of ciphertext), KEK version, caller principal, request-id, operation (unwrap/rewrap/rotate), and whether the operation used an emergency override. Retention: legal asked for 1 year for unwrap events.

sana: Any perf numbers we can point to? e.g., KMS latency + overhead for unwrap in our infra?

kevin: Typical unwrap latency ~50-150ms depending on clouds + network. With local cache hit rates >95% you only pay that occasionally. If you make DEKs per-object and TTL low, expect many unwraps.

jess: Small snippet for unwrap flow to include in the playbook: 
```
# pseudo
if cache.get(dek_id):
  return cache[dek_id]
dek_blob = db.fetch_encrypted_dek(dek_id)
dek_plain = kms.unwrap(kek_id, dek_blob)  # audited event emitted
cache.set(dek_id, dek_plain, ttl=jittered_ttl)
return dek_plain
```

ashok: Also recommend adding a background rewrap queue and a stale-detection metric: rewrap_backlog_count and rewrap_rate. Track time-to-zero after rotation.

sana: RBAC changes: we'll need a small change to CI role policies to remove broad kms:Decrypt and add more scoped grants. Also need an emergency access playbook with MFA and recorded approvals.

jess: + automated pager + audit email on any manual human decrypts. And require justification in the ticket.system for manual unwraps.

kevin: Don't forget to test: add a tabletop for KEK compromise, and a red-team scenario for DEK cache extraction. Measure time-to-detection and rewrap throughput.

sana: This is great — thanks. I'll draft a playbook and open a PR with default TTLs, splay settings, and the RBAC change. Will @ops-liz and @ashok for review.

ops-liz: happy to review — let's aim to land defaults behind a feature flag for private deployments. :thumbsup:
